quote:
When a mine falls silent beneath the earth, its loss is louder than any echo of triumph.  

The roar of a missile over a student hall reminds us that vengeance is a flame that shields no one but burns the past.  

A rocket that dreams of stars must first honor the gravity that keeps its feet on the ground.  

Allyship among great nations is a braided rope; once a strand frays, the whole sways.  

A disease’s threat may feel like an invisible storm—careful one must read the wind before heeding the clouds.  

When a nation casts off its guiding hand, the remaining banners must learn anew to catch the wind.  

A shipyard’s fury teaches that even the bravest of sparks may falter when touched by the sparks they attempt to tame.
